inspection_summary: Inspected all 4,488 splitlines from title through bibliography. The 88-page source is mathematically rich across its conceptual motivation, local and global trace constructions, cutoff arguments, RH-equivalence mechanism, and three technical appendices. Prose is coherent throughout; several displayed formulas are text-layer damaged, so formula-dependent units retain explicit representation warnings and are accepted only where surrounding prose fixes their role.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and contents
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Title, abstract, and navigation; the abstract states the absorption-spectrum and global-trace program.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the canonical critical/noncritical spectral split, the local-to-global trace plan, the open global boundary, and Hilbert–Polya/random-matrix motivation.

sections_inspected.label: I Quantum chaos and the hypothetical Riemann flow
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Compares periodic-orbit and Euler-product expansions to derive prime-orbit, period, instability, symmetry, and sign constraints.

sections_inspected.label: II Algebraic Geometry and global fields of nonzero characteristic
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses the function-field Frobenius/cohomology dictionary to motivate absorption, cohomological sign, and the idele-class acting group.

sections_inspected.label: III Spectral interpretation of critical zeros
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs the Adele-class Hilbert space, embeds it into the regular representation, and identifies critical zeros in the cokernel spectrum.

sections_inspected.label: IV Distribution trace formula for flows
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops fixed-point and periodic-orbit distributional trace contributions for smooth flows.

sections_inspected.label: V Local-field multiplicative action
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Makes the local fixed-point denominator rigorous using distributions, dual cutoffs, symbols, and a canonically normalized principal value.

sections_inspected.label: VI Global formal trace computation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies global fixed loci with place hyperplanes and formally recovers the Weil explicit distribution.

sections_inspected.label: VII S-local trace formula
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Proves a rigorous trace formula on non-type-I S-local Adele quotients and controls the cutoff error.

sections_inspected.label: VIII Global trace and elimination of delta
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the delta-free cutoff, relates its trace formula to positivity and RH, treats resonances and the Archimedean cutoff, and returns to zero counting.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix I Proof of theorem 1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Supplies homogeneous-distribution, Poisson-summation, Sobolev, and cokernel-annihilator machinery underlying the spectral theorem.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix II Explicit formulas
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Rewrites Weil's explicit formula in trace notation and proves agreement of local principal-value normalizations.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix III Distribution trace formulas
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Provides coordinate-free density, wave-front, kernel, transversality, and pushforward foundations for the flow trace formula.

sections_inspected.label: Bibliography
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: References only; no independent semantic unit selected.

accepted_units.title: Zeros as absorption lines and the global trace boundary
accepted_units.why_material: Distinguishes critical zeros appearing directly from noncritical zeros appearing through harmonic-potential resonances, locates both in an Adele-class trace formula, and states that the unproved global trace formula is equivalent to RH for all Grössencharakter L-functions.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span; it is a self-contained programmatic overview and clearly separates proved local/S-local results from the open global assertion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant; notation for Adele and idele classes is recoverable from the text.

accepted_units.title: Naturality criterion for a Hilbert–Polya realization
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why selfadjointness or positivity could relocate RH, connects the proposal to Selberg and zero-spacing statistics, and insists that a genuine construction not smuggle the zeros or zeta function into its definition.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the counting-function split, unfolding to unit mean spacing, and GUE evidence needed for the naturality demand.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several displayed asymptotics are formula-dependent but legible enough with the prose.

accepted_units.title: Periodic-orbit constraints on a hypothetical Riemann flow
accepted_units.why_material: Comparing semiclassical periodic-orbit and Euler-product oscillations forces primes as primitive orbits, logarithmic periods and instability exponents, absence of time reversal, while exposing the unresolved overall sign and finite-iterate denominator mismatches.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span; it begins inside the quantum-chaos setup and therefore receives an explicit v2 context repair to lines 196–297.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dense and dependent on OCR-affected displayed equations (6) and (7); the enumerated conclusions and mismatches are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Function-field geometry turns the spectral sign into cohomology
accepted_units.why_material: Transfers zeros, functional equation, explicit formulas, and RH to Frobenius cohomology, duality, Lefschetz, and positivity; the alternating cohomological sign motivates a negative or absorption spectrum and the idele class group as the acting symmetry.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the global-field definition and periodic Frobenius-orbit interpretation needed to justify the transfer rather than merely list a dictionary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The dictionary table and Lefschetz formula are partially layout-sensitive, but the surrounding prose determines the correspondences.

accepted_units.title: Adele-class quotient and the two vanishing conditions
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs X=A/k* as the noncommutative quotient, explains why quotient functions are formed through orbit sums, and derives f(0)=0 and integral f=0 as the conditions removing the fixed-origin and small-scale divergences before completion.
accepted_units.context_note: The universal-cover analogy and the weighted norm are retained because they explain both quotienting and the artificial Sobolev parameter.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Orbit-sum and norm formulas are necessary; text extraction splits some displays but the definitions remain recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Embedding into the regular representation and taking a cokernel
accepted_units.why_material: The orbit-sum map E, with its square-root modular factor, embeds the Adele-class space equivariantly into a weighted regular representation; its invariant cokernel supplies the negative cohomological Polya–Hilbert space.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the two-dimensional C plus Tate-twist supplement, the modular normalization, and the noncanonical compact-times-module splitting.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent but supported by explicit measure comparison and equivariance prose.

accepted_units.title: Critical zeros as spectrum of the cokernel generator
accepted_units.why_material: Decomposes by compact characters, obtains a generator with imaginary spectrum, and states that its discrete spectral points are exactly critical-line L-function zeros with a delta-controlled multiplicity; the trace corollary and Jordan warning expose both value and limitation.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains resolvents, theorem, trace corollary, independence from prior definition of L, and the effect of changing the noncanonical splitting.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The theorem statement is legible; multiplicity inequalities and Fourier-transform displays should be checked against the scan before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Formal character from exact sequences and the need for regularization
accepted_units.why_material: Combines the two exact sequences to express the Adele-class character as trivial and Tate terms minus the critical-zero spectrum, while explicitly identifying the divergent regular-representation trace and the need to regularize it by fixed-point methods.
accepted_units.context_note: Closes Section III and states the bridge to the later cutoff construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact-sequence and formal-trace displays are central; infinity notation signals formal rather than established equality.

accepted_units.title: Distributional Lefschetz trace from transverse fixed points
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how restricting an operator kernel to the diagonal turns transversality into isolated fixed-point contributions weighted by the inverse determinant, then recovers the alternating cohomological Lefschetz trace.
accepted_units.context_note: The coordinate-free details are deferred to Appendix III but the mechanism is complete here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on delta-kernel and determinant formulas that are readable in the extraction.

accepted_units.title: From fixed points to zeros and periodic orbits of a flow
accepted_units.why_material: Generalizes the distributional trace to a one-parameter flow, separates fixed zeros from periodic orbits, and packages both using isotropy groups, covolume-normalized Haar measures, and transverse return maps.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the one-dimensional scaling example that becomes the local-field template.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula and geometric-notation dependent; Appendix III supplies a second derivation.

accepted_units.title: Fourier control of the local fixed-point denominator
accepted_units.why_material: For multiplication on an arbitrary local field, computes the fixed-point contribution |1−lambda|^{-1} and justifies the product of delta distributions by convolving their Fourier transforms, clarifying why the transverse case is well-defined.
accepted_units.context_note: Ends exactly where the nontransverse h(1) case forces the cutoff theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-dependent; prose fixes the convolution-of-line-measures argument despite layout damage.

accepted_units.title: Dual cutoff and canonical local principal value
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces infrared and Fourier-conjugate ultraviolet projections and states a trace asymptotic with a universal logarithmic divergence plus a principal value uniquely normalized by vanishing of its Fourier transform at one.
accepted_units.context_note: The full theorem statement is retained before its longer proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prime on log and the principal-value display are formula-sensitive and should be scan-verified for exact constants.

accepted_units.title: Symbol calculus converts cutoff trace to the principal value
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the Schwartz kernel symbol, Parseval, the product variable x·xi, and the Fourier transform of −log|u| to split the cutoff trace into its logarithmic leading term and the canonical local distribution.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the decay estimate that removes the truncated tail and the comparison with Weil's normalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dense with some damaged displays; conceptual chain is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Places as global fixed hyperplanes with local transverse actions
accepted_units.why_material: Solves the fixed-point equation on the Adele-class quotient: nontrivial stabilizers occur on place-indexed hyperplanes, each generic isotropy is the embedded local multiplicative group, and the transverse action is precisely local scaling.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the nonclosed-orbit/closed-hyperplane distinction and covolume-one measure normalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose and quotient notation are sufficient; local-field integral display carries the final contribution.

accepted_units.title: Formal global trace recovers Weil but remains nonrigorous
accepted_units.why_material: Summing placewise fixed contributions yields Weil's explicit distribution, exposes the distinction between critical-only and all-zero spectral sides, and argues that positivity is Lefschetz/permutation-like rather than semiclassical quantization; cutoff and delta remain explicit obstacles.
accepted_units.context_note: The inversion convention for h and the h(1)=0 restriction are included to prevent a false unconditional trace identity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive, especially the divergent h(1) term; logical limitations are clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: S-local non-type-I quotient with a unitary Fourier transform
accepted_units.why_material: Reduces the global problem to a finite set of places while retaining non-type-I orbit behavior, constructs L2(X_S) without delta, and proves that Fourier transformation is unitary by an exponentially convergent S-unit correlation sum.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the concrete three-place example and the dual cutoff definition needed for Theorem 4.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Norm and lattice estimates are formula-dependent; prose identifies their analytic role.

accepted_units.title: Rigorous S-local trace formula
accepted_units.why_material: States that the dual-cutoff trace on the S-local quotient equals the logarithmic identity contribution plus the sum of canonically normalized local Weil terms for every place in S.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the central proved finite-place result and retains all hypotheses and normalizations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed asymptotic is essential and should be scan-checked for prime marks and inversions.

accepted_units.title: Selberg-style quotient trace decomposes into placewise logarithms
accepted_units.why_material: Lifts the quotient test function to ideles, unfolds the trace over S-units, passes to symbols, and decomposes log|u| into local logarithms so the global quotient trace becomes a finite sum of local principal values.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the finiteness argument for which S-units meet support and isolates the sole remaining cutoff-tail estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very formula-dense; source prose preserves the sequence of reductions but exact identities need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Geometric summability and rapid decay of the cutoff error
accepted_units.why_material: Uses a word metric on S-units, fractional-difference convolution norms, and Schwartz decay to prove geometric summability in the unit variable and faster-than-any-power decay in the cutoff.
accepted_units.context_note: This technical unit closes the gap between the formal place decomposition and the rigorous asymptotic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Estimate-heavy and OCR-sensitive; qualitative dependencies and conclusion are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Cutoff replaces delta and admits all zeros canonically
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why the weighted space gives artificial multiplicities and suppresses off-line zeros, then replaces it with the delta-zero Hilbert space and a cutoff whose spectral side contains critical zeros directly and noncritical zeros as resonances.
accepted_units.context_note: Concise transition unit stating the design criterion for the entire global section.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant.

accepted_units.title: Function-field cutoff as an intersection of support and Fourier support
accepted_units.why_material: Analyzes the pair of projections by compact characters, computes their trace, constructs enough independent translated test vectors to identify their intersection, and obtains exact commutation and dimension control in positive characteristic.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes conductor/genus corrections and the cyclicity argument because they certify that the lower bound exhausts the intersection.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dense; exact conductor and dimension constants need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: S-independent global cutoff and the remaining trace conjecture
accepted_units.why_material: Recasts the S-local result using the projection onto functions and Fourier transforms supported below the cutoff, explains stabilization as S grows, and isolates the unproved arbitrary-h global trace formula even in positive characteristic.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves the distinction between the proved supported-on-C_{k,1} case and the desired full formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Trace asymptotic and support conditions are readable but formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Global cutoff trace is equivalent to RH
accepted_units.why_material: States Theorem 5 and proves the trace-to-RH direction by embedding the cutoff subspace into a regular-representation window; the positive operator difference converges to the Weil distribution, so trace validity forces its positive type.
accepted_units.context_note: The reverse implication is separated into the harmonic-measure unit that follows.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Projection inequalities and distribution formulas are essential; prose explicitly describes the positivity logic.

accepted_units.title: Harmonic measure turns off-line zeros into resonances
accepted_units.why_material: Computes the limit of the positive cutoff-difference distributions from zero constraints: critical zeros give point masses on the spectral line, while off-line zeros contribute their Poisson/harmonic measures with full multiplicity.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the finite-dimensional shift model that explains the limit and supplies the RH-to-trace implication.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The lemma's displayed sum is extraction-damaged, but the subsequent prose unambiguously states critical versus noncritical behavior.

accepted_units.title: Prolate spheroidal functions repair the Archimedean support obstruction
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why exact joint compact support fails at real places and replaces intersection by the near-one eigenspace of the time-frequency limiting operator, controlled by a commuting differential operator and a sharp transition near the phase-space dimension.
accepted_units.context_note: The projector-angle viewpoint connects the function-field exact intersection to the number-field approximate one.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Spectral thresholds and constants are formula-dependent; the qualitative transition is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Zero counting appears as a deficit of cutoff states
accepted_units.why_material: Counts the phase-space region for the scaling Hamiltonian under simultaneous position, momentum, and energy cutoffs, recovering the smooth zero-counting term with the negative sign appropriate to an absorption spectrum and interpreting it as failure of surjectivity of the orbit-sum map.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes normalization at the real place and clearly labels the additional oscillatory terms as requiring the finer trace formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Area and normalization formulas are central and should be scan-verified for constants.

accepted_units.title: The cutoff angle spectrum also governs random-matrix gap probabilities
accepted_units.why_material: Relates eigenvalues of the projector-angle/time-frequency operator to the Fredholm-product description of large-matrix eigenvalue counts, linking the cutoff construction back to zero statistics.
accepted_units.context_note: A compact but nonredundant bridge between two appearances of the same operator spectrum.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Notation-heavy and formula-dependent; prose states the relationship.

accepted_units.title: Quotienting through the inner product as gauge removal
accepted_units.why_material: Compares the Adele-class completion with construction of physical Hilbert spaces in gauge theory: invariance directions disappear in the seminorm rather than by selecting representatives.
accepted_units.context_note: Short general remark with a reusable quotient mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-only.

accepted_units.title: Noncommutative Adele classes as an Archimedean Frobenius setting
accepted_units.why_material: Connects the idele connected component to type-III factor structure, emphasizes that quotienting destroys linear dimension products in favor of sums, and identifies the idele action on Adele classes as the class-field-theoretic analogue of Frobenius.
accepted_units.context_note: Clearly presented as a proposed interpretation, not an established proof mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant.

accepted_units.title: Why state counting and imported positivity can miss absorption
accepted_units.why_material: Critiques routes that obtain the sign by deleting regions or define an inner product directly from the Weil distribution, distinguishing explanation of the distribution from merely assuming its positivity.
accepted_units.context_note: Useful negative evidence about circular or sign-mismatched formulations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-only.

accepted_units.title: Proposed extension from GL(1) to matrix Adele classes
accepted_units.why_material: Suggests replacing the Adele-class space by matrices modulo GL_n(k), reports only preliminary spectral evidence, and correctly leaves the higher-rank Lefschetz formula as the next unresolved step.
accepted_units.context_note: Retained as a bounded research direction, not a completed generalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-only.

accepted_units.title: L-functions normalize global homogeneous distributions
accepted_units.why_material: Builds local homogeneous distributions, normalizes unramified factors, forms their restricted tensor product, and shows that the Euler-product L-function is exactly the scalar relating the convergent global integral to the holomorphic normalized distribution.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides the analytic factorization later used to turn zeros of L into annihilators of the orbit-sum range.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Long and formula-dense; local normalization and Euler-factor displays require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Poisson summation gives inversion and rapid decay of the orbit sum
accepted_units.why_material: Uses self-duality of the global-field lattice to derive E(f)(x)=E(f-hat)(1/x) on the two-vanishing-condition space, then proves rapid decay at both ends and extends the L-factor identity into the half-plane.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the exact bridge from Tate–Iwasawa analysis to a Hilbert-space range condition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Poisson and Mellin formulas are central; prose supplies the convergence argument.

accepted_units.title: Band-limited approximate units in weighted regular representations
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs uniformly bounded approximate identities with compact Fourier support in weighted translation spaces and transports them to the idele class group, allowing the cokernel analysis to reduce to compact spectral support.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the dual weighted-space pairing and growth bound needed for the later distribution argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Estimate-dependent but extraction is sufficiently coherent.

accepted_units.title: Zeros characterize the annihilator of the orbit-sum range
accepted_units.why_material: Decomposes the dual by compact characters, Mellin-transforms annihilators of Im(E), uses L(1/2+it) times the transformed distribution equals zero, and identifies the allowed delta derivatives with zero multiplicity and Sobolev order, yielding the cokernel generator's Jordan spectrum.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the converse construction from derivatives of homogeneous distributions, so the spectral characterization is bidirectional.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extremely formula-sensitive; the distribution-support logic is clear, but multiplicity bounds should be verified from the scan.

accepted_units.title: Schwartz convolution is trace class with zero sum trace
accepted_units.why_material: Uses compact Fourier localization and zero-density growth to show Schwartz averages of the cokernel representation are trace class and computes their trace as the critical-zero sum with theorem-controlled multiplicity.
accepted_units.context_note: Completes the proof package for the preliminary spectral interpretation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula and multiplicity notation are essential.

accepted_units.title: Weil distribution as global term minus local principal values
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the zero sum and Weil distribution, decomposes it into discriminant, global, and placewise local terms, and records the normalized local principal values whose positivity is equivalent to RH.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the test-function growth hypotheses and field-dependent normalization context.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dense and sensitive to Archimedean principal-value conventions.

accepted_units.title: Rewriting Weil's explicit formula in trace-test notation
accepted_units.why_material: Changes variables from radial F to the trace test function h, identifies Mellin transforms with character Fourier transforms, and rewrites the zero sum as trivial terms minus placewise fixed-point integrals, valid initially on the stated test class and unconditionally when h(1)=0.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the exact algebraic bridge between the number-theoretic explicit formula and the geometric trace expression.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Inversion and half-power conventions are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Local cutoff principal values agree with Weil's
accepted_units.why_material: Checks non-Archimedean, real, and complex local fields separately, using normalized basic characters and Fourier transforms of −log|u| to show that the cutoff-selected principal value is exactly Weil's local prescription.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the complex-plane area computation because it closes the last normalization case rather than merely asserting agreement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Constant-heavy and OCR-sensitive; all exact constants require scan verification before reuse.

accepted_units.title: Changing the additive character shifts only the identity term
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how rescaling the basic additive character changes the selfdual Fourier transform and adds log|lambda| at the identity; summing local differential-idele shifts cancels the discriminant term and yields the global explicit formula in the cutoff normalization.
accepted_units.context_note: Ends with Theorem 6, the precise global formula required by the main trace discussion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent, especially selfdual-measure scaling and the final zero sum.

accepted_units.title: Canonical Haar measure for modulated groups
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the unique Haar normalization from logarithmic growth of the module range, treats continuous and discrete ranges, and proves compatibility with quotienting by compact subgroups.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides the common normalization silently used for local isotropy and global idele-class measures.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Elementary formulas are legible.

accepted_units.title: Densities, delta sections, and transverse pullback
accepted_units.why_material: Defines generalized bundle sections, pushforward and pullback, states the wave-front transversality condition, and shows that a delta section on a submanifold pulls back to the delta section on its transverse inverse image.
accepted_units.context_note: Supplies the coordinate-free legality of restricting a trace kernel to a diagonal.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Geometric bundle notation is extraction-sensitive but prose is coherent.

accepted_units.title: A pullback operator has the graph delta as kernel
accepted_units.why_material: Applies the Schwartz kernel theorem to a smooth map and canonically identifies the symbol of its graph-supported delta distribution, justifying the familiar kernel delta(y−f(x)) without coordinates.
accepted_units.context_note: A compact foundation for every later fixed-point trace restriction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on conormal-bundle notation and the displayed kernel identity.

accepted_units.title: Poincaré transversality yields periodic-orbit and zero contributions
accepted_units.why_material: Derives that diagonal/graph transversality is invertibility of one minus the transverse return map, computes the pulled-back symbol, and pushes it to time to obtain covolume-weighted periodic-orbit terms and determinant-weighted fixed-zero terms in a single isotropy formula.
accepted_units.context_note: This appendix derivation independently certifies the main Section IV formula under its exact hypotheses.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula- and geometry-dependent; text is coherent though several displays are layout-damaged.

v1_context_repairs.reason: The immutable span starts at line 235 in the middle of the quantum-chaos argument. Lines 196–234 define the Hamiltonian spectral setting, the average/oscillatory split, time reversal, and the chaotic isolated-orbit hypothesis needed to interpret the semiclassical formula and its comparison with the Euler product.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Why the negative sign selects absorption rather than emission
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The periodic-orbit minus-sign obstruction and the alternating cohomological Lefschetz sign jointly motivate realizing zeros as missing states in a cokernel, with off-line zeros represented resonantly.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a source-grounded motivation and architecture, not a proof that the global trace formula or RH holds.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From quotient semantics to a zero-bearing cokernel
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Quotienting Adele functions by k* through a seminorm produces an orbit-sum embedding into a regular representation, and the missing quotient range carries the critical-zero spectrum.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The preliminary construction uses the artificial Sobolev parameter and sees only critical-line zeros directly.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Local fixed-point mechanics assemble the Weil distribution
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Transverse fixed-point denominators for local multiplicative actions become placewise contributions because global fixed loci are place hyperplanes, and the S-local cutoff rigorously realizes their finite sum.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The passage from every finite S to the unrestricted global trace remains a separate unproved step.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The cutoff makes RH a positivity statement about missing states
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: After removing delta, the difference between a regular-representation window and the joint support/Fourier-support subspace is positive; its limit is the Weil distribution, with off-line zeros spread by harmonic measure, so the asserted global trace is equivalent to RH.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Equivalence does not supply the missing proof of the global trace, and the detailed construction is first established in positive characteristic.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Time-frequency concentration replaces impossible Archimedean compact support
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: At real places, prolate-spheroidal concentration supplies an approximate joint cutoff whose effective dimension matches phase-space area; the deficit realizes the smooth zero count and the same angle spectrum connects to random-matrix gaps.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The semiclassical count does not by itself recover the oscillatory zero term or prove spectral convergence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Cutoff normalization exactly matches the number-theoretic explicit formula
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The Fourier-vanishing local principal value chosen by the operator cutoff agrees place by place with Weil's normalization, while additive-character shifts account exactly for the differential-idele term in the global formula.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several constants are formula-layer sensitive and require scan verification before exact computational reuse.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic continuation becomes a spectral annihilator condition
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Poisson summation and homogeneous distributions factor the orbit-sum Mellin transform by L; band-limited approximation then makes zeros, their orders, and allowed distribution derivatives precisely characterize the cokernel spectrum and trace.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The Sobolev exponent truncates observed multiplicity and this appendix result is the preliminary critical-line model, not the later delta-free global theorem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Microlocal transversality is the rigorous source of orbit weights
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Wave-front-safe pullback of the graph delta to the diagonal is valid exactly when one minus the Poincaré return map is invertible, and its symbol produces the determinant and covolume weights in the flow trace.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The derivation assumes the stated transversality and excludes the identity-time singularity by requiring the test function to vanish at zero.
